You are being evaluated on Continual-ARC, a lifelong stream of ARC-style grid puzzles.
Each puzzle instance has a task id and a test input grid. Tasks recur across the
stream with fresh inputs. Each instance is a separate conversation: the next one
starts without this one's messages.

On every message you must choose exactly one action and put it as a JSON object
on the last line of your reply:

Each demo request returns one more input-output pair of the task, up to the demo cap shown

instance is over when a submission is correct or when the attempt cap is reached, and
reaching the cap is charged the full cap. Feedback on a submission is only
correct/incorrect. There is no way to abandon an instance, and finish is refused until

# Continual-ARC horizontal gap insertion

Use when task demos show sparse same-color markers along rows and output inserts another color into horizontal gaps.

## Verified pattern
A demonstrated transformation preserves markers and fills background cells strictly between consecutive marker positions in the same row. In the reference demonstration, markers were color 4 on background 9 and every intervening gap cell became 2. The same pattern applied to a test with markers 0 on background 3, using insertion color 2. Rows without at least two markers remain unchanged; cells outside spans remain unchanged. Dimensions are preserved.

## Procedure
1. Identify marker, background, and insertion colors from the current task's demos; do not carry colors over from another task.
2. For each row, find marker positions. For each consecutive pair, fill only background cells strictly between them with the demonstrated insertion color.
3. Preserve markers, cells outside spans, and rows with fewer than two markers.
4. Do not extend this rule vertically or beyond marker-bounded spans unless current-task demos establish that behavior.
5. Verify dimensions and ensure no unintended edits before submitting.

## Additional confirmed configuration
A further task used marker 3 on background 6 with insertion color 2. Across irregular, staggered rows, every background cell between each pair of consecutive horizontal markers changed to 2, while all other cells remained unchanged. This confirms that row eligibility is independent: apply the row rule to every row containing at least two markers, even when adjacent rows have different patterns or a marker appears vertically aligned elsewhere.

## Additional confirmed configuration
A current task used marker 6 on background 7 with insertion color 2. Across rows with varying marker counts and staggered positions, every background cell strictly between consecutive markers in each row changed to 2; markers and all outside cells were preserved. This further confirms row-wise, consecutive-marker gap filling with task-specific colors.

## Task-specific instance record: task-8c8e1d50
The task used background 5, marker 0, and inserted color 2. Its 9×21 demo had background 3, marker 8, and inserted color 2; in both, fill only row-wise background cells strictly between consecutive same-row markers. This correctly solved the 12×10 test with zero wrong submissions. This further confirms palette independence and confirms no vertical fill despite aligned markers. The test rows with qualifying marker sets filled their bounded horizontal intervals; isolated/no-marker rows stayed unchanged.

## Important counterexample / resolved selective-gap family
A recurring task family (including task-71ededcc) is NOT simple blanket gap-fill on every axis. Infer from demos which orientation/lines qualify. In demonstrated examples, background 1 or 0, marker color 3/9 or 0, inserted color 2. Rule: for each row and column independently, if its marker cells include at least one adjacent pair (a contiguous run of >=2 markers), fill background cells lying between the outermost markers on that same line with 2; preserve markers and outside cells. Do not fill an otherwise marker-bounded line if its markers are all isolated (no adjacent marker pair). This distinction explains why earlier broad interpolation guesses were wrong.

For task-71ededcc's demos, only rows with adjacent marker runs and columns with adjacent marker runs were completed: demo 1's qualifying rows/columns extend inserted 2s across their marker extrema, while isolated-marker-only lines remain unchanged. The accepted 12×22 test output filled the top and bottom marker-run rows horizontally across their outermost markers, plus vertical marker-run column(s) between their extrema; isolated-only row/columns were untouched. At demo 3, color-3 horizontal top and bottom rows have contiguous marker pairs, and the interior vertical boundary columns have contiguous runs; inserted 2 fills intervening gaps. This is a task-family rule, not a universal coordinate template.

The ordinary horizontal-gap rule remains applicable when demos show all rows with >=2 markers qualify. For selective 2D completion, validate against every demo cellwise and distinguish an adjacent marker pair from merely multiple isolated markers on a line.

## Task-71ededcc recurrence — unresolved, do not reuse failed predictions
A recurrence with test grid 12×18 (background 8, markers 4) was presented with seven demonstrations and eight attempts. All eight submissions failed. It is not a solved rule; use this only as a strong warning and evidence record. Do not repeat the failed outputs or assume the rule is ordinary gap filling, all-axis interpolation, contiguous-pair line filling, or simple transfer from the first demos.

Demos across palettes show marker color varying by example and inserted color 2. Patterns can trigger selective recoloring on rows and columns, and even a complex solid rectangular border (demo 4) produced changes at selected single cells but not a blanket fill. Demo 7's near-solid 4 rectangle with two vertical 0 bars had just one 0→2 change at row 14, column 12. Thus a local shape/object-context selector exists, and rules guessed from aligned marker gaps alone are insufficient.

For the test, markers occupy: row2 c6,c12; row3 c13; row4 c13; row5 c6,c7,c8,c10,c11,c12; row7 c6; row8 c13; row10 c6,c12,c13. Eight failed submissions explored broad horizontal fills and combinations of vertical fills in c6/c12/c13, but none was accepted. In particular, all variants based on filling the row5 gap and row10 gap (with or without vertical additions) were rejected. Treat any asserted exact target output as unknown. Future recurrence: request informative demos early, map all changed cells and invariants, infer the selector that identifies target cells, and avoid near-duplicate submissions.
## Evidence scope
This rule has been demonstrated across several color configurations: marker 4 on background 9 filled with 2; marker 6 on background 3 filled with 2; marker 0 on background 3 filled with 2; and marker 8 on background 9 filled with 2. In the latter task, a 13×21 demo and a 27×15 test showed scattered marker-8 positions; fill each same-row gap between consecutive markers with 2, preserving marker cells and all cells outside the bounded gaps. Rows with only one marker remain unchanged. This instance was accepted with that exact transformation. Treat it as a candidate, not a universal ARC rule; verify applicability from each task's demos. ## When to Use
Use when a grid contains a compact color sequence-bar repeated across adjacent rows or columns, alongside one or more copies of a distinctive non-rectangular mask in separate colors.

# Sequence-colored motif stacking

Use when a grid contains a compact colored sequence-bar (same sequence repeated across several adjacent rows/columns), plus one or more copies of a distinctive non-rectangular mask in separate colors.

## Rule supported by solved task-3bf58883
The repeated stripe sequence gives the ordered colors for a vertical stack of copies of a 3-row mask. The mask is the distinctive pattern (in the solved demos, the 3-row shape colored 1). Tile that exact occupancy pattern vertically, one 3-row band per sequence color, preserving the motif's columns and ordering the bands top-to-bottom according to the sequence encoded by the color bar. The original motif band is included at the position corresponding to its own color. Remove the encoding bar and other redundant motif-color copies; background remains unchanged.

Evidence:
- Demo 1: vertical bar colors [4,1,6]; the 3-row mask became bands 4,1,6 from top to bottom. Its original 1 band was preserved in the middle; a 6 copy already at the bottom was consistent.
- Demo 2: vertical bar [7,2,1,3]; same 3-row mask repeated top-to-bottom in exactly those colors, including the pre-existing 2 and 1 mask copies.
- Solved test: horizontal repeated row sequence [2,3,1,8,7] was read left-to-right. The 3-row mask was stacked as bands 2,3,1,8,7 in that top-to-bottom order, and the submission was confirmed correct.

## Applying the rule
1. Identify the repeated stripe/bar: its same ordered colors across repeated adjacent rows means a vertical sequence; a repeated ordered sequence across columns means horizontal. In the solved instance, rows each repeated the same left-to-right sequence.
2. Identify the common sparse occupancy mask, usually from the color-1 motif. Ignore its color when comparing copies; compare coordinates/shape.
3. Read sequence colors in stripe order. Determine whether a bar is horizontal or vertical from demos; do not infer direction from a single example if ambiguous.
4. Produce one mask copy per sequence color, with each consecutive copy occupying one motif-height band, and preserve the motif's horizontal placement. Ensure output height accommodates all bands. In demonstrated cases, the stack begins at row 0 and each band is three rows high.
5. Do not retain the color key/stripe unless demos explicitly show it in the output. Preserve background elsewhere.
6. Validate row count and width carefully: prior failed attempts on task-3bf58883 were invalid ARC grids due to omitted trailing zeros, not a rejected transformation. For width 15, every row must have exactly 15 values; for width 14, exactly 14.

## Caution
Treat mask size, stack anchoring, sequence direction, whether extra preexisting mask copies are retained, and treatment of leftover rows/columns as demo-dependent. This is an evidence-backed task family, not a universal ARC rule. # Continual-ARC largest-patch color code

## Trigger
A large noisy grid contains several spatially localized dense monochromatic regions, and examples show a small fixed output grid uniformly filled with one patch color.

## Supported rule
For task family `task-c6218526`, output is a 3×3 grid filled uniformly with the color belonging to the largest dense patch/object by cell count. Two demos produced uniform grids colored 4 and 3; in each, that color's dense region was the largest. A held-out test was correctly answered with a uniform 3×3 of color 5.

## Procedure
1. Separate coherent dense patches from the surrounding noise. Do not count scattered isolated cells of the same color as patch area unless spatially connected/coherent.
2. Tally candidate patch cell counts, including irregular boundaries, and compare all candidate colors.
3. Choose the color of the largest patch and emit a 3×3 grid uniformly filled with it, when demos confirm the encoding.
4. Validate output dimensions and uniformity.

## Caution
